verdict.rationale: Google Drive documents permissions on every file, folder and shared drive, with roles owner, organizer, fileOrganizer, writer, commenter and reader. The user-facing docs cover edit, comment and view-only controls and state that folder access is inherited by all files within it. missing for 10: detailed inheritance docs (overriding or restricting inherited access, shared-drive inheritance nuances), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, permissions are granular — folder- and file-level roles (viewer/commenter/editor/owner) with inheritance behavior documented

citations.quote: Each resource identifies the permission for a specific type (user, group, domain, anyone) and role (owner, organizer, fileOrganizer, writer, commenter, reader).
Every Google Drive file, folder, and shared drive has associated `permissions` resources.
Access you apply to a folder is inherited by all files within it.
When you share from Google Drive, you can control whether people can edit, comment on, or only open the file.
A permission grants a user, group, domain, or the world access to a file or a folder hierarchy.
